To implement a systematic equity trading strategy focused on low-volatility tilting in the Indian market, we aim to exploit the empirical phenomenon where low-volatility stocks tend to outperform high-volatility stocks over time. This effect is often attributed to risk aversion among investors and the pricing of risk by the market.

The rationale behind this persistence is that lower volatility can be seen as a proxy for better risk management and more stable earnings, which historically have translated into higher returns due to reduced downside risk. Additionally, during periods of market stress or uncertainty, low-volatility stocks tend to exhibit less price fluctuation, providing a stabilizing effect.

Our strategy would involve constructing an index or portfolio that weights stocks based on their historical volatility, favoring lower volatility names. Specifically, we could rank stocks by their historical standard deviation over the past year and construct a long-short portfolio where low-volatility stocks are overrepresented in the long positions while high-volatility stocks are underrepresented or shorted. This rule would continuously rebalance to maintain optimal exposure to low-volatility stocks, capturing potential outperformance while managing risk effectively.

The signal for this strategy is based on historical volatility. Specifically, compute the 1-year historical standard deviation of daily returns for each stock using the closing prices from the past year. Rank stocks by their calculated volatility, with lower volatility stocks receiving higher ranks. On any given day, construct a long-short portfolio where stocks in the lowest volatility quartile are overrepresented in long positions, while those in the highest volatility quartile are underrepresented or shorted. This ranking and portfolio construction process is performed daily to ensure continuous rebalancing.

For this systematic equity strategy focused on low-volatility tilting in the Indian market, we recommend holding a portfolio of approximately 30-50 stocks. The positions are dynamically rebalanced daily based on historical volatility rankings. Low-volatility stocks (bottom quartile) are overweighted by 15-20%, while high-volatility stocks (top quartile) are underweighted or shorted by up to 5%. Position sizes are constrained such that no single stock can represent more than 3% of the portfolio, and the total short position is limited to 10% of the portfolio value to manage risk effectively. Loss limits are set at a maximum drawdown threshold of -10%, ensuring capital preservation while capturing potential outperformance from low-volatility stocks.
